overall_notes: All three P2 NHL SOG overs use fresh 4:50–4:51 PM ET prices at the exact 1.5 line with per-book devig medians and at least three books, so none trigger line-mismatch, single-book, or stale-price vetoes. The drafter flags B2B, recent cold streaks, and Tippett’s minutes without hiding them; those are priced risks, not reasoning gaps. Default veto stance: keep all legs.

votes.reasoning: Carlsson’s 1.5 SOG over is backed by four books near -180 with a 60.7% median devig, Sennecke IR concentrating top-six offense, and 7/10 L10 clears with 2.0 SOG average. Back-to-back and three 1-shot games are real but explicitly in the write-up. I’d cut only if the app line diverges from 1.5 or repricing drops below two exact-line books.

Stenberg meets the multi-book rule at 1.5 with a 58.3% median and a rested SJ matchup vs SEA on a B2B, with forward absences supporting his top-six role. The last two 1-SOG games are the main miss path but are called out. A cut would need a stale or single-book price, or a same-player recent miss with an unchanged line—none apply.

Tippett’s volume profile (6/10 over 1.5, 2.3 avg, hot last three) and thin MTL defense support the over despite PHI B2B and 11–15 minute TOI dips that the drafter already weighs. Three books at -190 on 1.5 with 61.1% median is not a methodology error. Role or ice-time collapse pre-game would be the main reason to reconsider, not a panel veto tag.
